newsitem.title: UK: EMI buys 50 pct of classic Motown songs.
newsitem.headline: EMI buys 50 pct of classic Motown songs.

text.p: British music company EMI Group Plc said on Tuesday that it had bought a 50 percent stake in the Jobete companies which control the back catalogue of classic Motown soul songs for $132 million in cash.
EMI has also contracted to administer the music catalogues of the companies worldwide for an extended period.
The Jobete companies, Jobete Music Co., Inc and Stone Diamond Music Corporation, are owned by Motown founder Berry Gordy and his sister Esther Edwards.

The catalogue includes such standards as Marvin Gaye's "I Heard It Through the Grapevine", The Temptations' "My Girl", Stevie Wonder's "I Just Called to Say I Love You" and "You Are the Sunshine of My Life", along with the songs of Smokey Robinson and the Miracles, Diana Ross and the Supremes, the Four Tops, the Jackson Five, Lionel Ritchie and the Commodores.
EMI, Gordy and Edwards have entered an agreement which may require EMI Music Publishing to buy the rest of the Jobete companies for a maximum $250 million.
EMI said it expects to improve significantly the performance of the Jobete companies in their first full year.
Jobete Music Co was formed by Berry Gordy in 1959 and became the music publishing affiliate to his Motown Records, which is now owned by PolyGram NV.
